es: Redactar avisos y consejos de seguridad con unless, provided that / as long as, in case y had better, usando presente tras la conjunción y verbo base tras had better.

teaching.en: Do not start the climb unless the forecast is clear, because the route becomes hazardous once the rocks are wet and the wind picks up.
teaching.es: No empieces la subida a menos que el pronóstico esté despejado, porque la ruta se vuelve peligrosa cuando las rocas están mojadas y el viento aumenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Unless ya significa «si no»: no se le añade otra negación. Hazardous = peligroso, con sentido de riesgo real.
segments: Do not start the climb unless the forecast is clear, because the route
becomes hazardous once the rocks are wet and the wind picks up.
teaching.audioText: Do not start the climb unless the forecast is clear, because the route becomes hazardous once the rocks are wet and the wind picks up.

teaching.en: You may camp beside the shelter provided that you leave no trace, and a small stove is fine as long as the wind stays light.
teaching.es: Puedes acampar junto al refugio siempre que no dejes huella, y un hornillo pequeño está bien mientras el viento se mantenga suave.
teaching.explanationEs: Provided that / as long as + presente: condición necesaria; no se usa will detrás.
segments: You may camp beside the shelter provided that you leave no trace, and
a small stove is fine as long as the wind stays light.
teaching.audioText: You may camp beside the shelter provided that you leave no trace, and a small stove is fine as long as the wind stays light.

teaching.en: Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down after dark, since the path is not lit at any point.
teaching.es: Lleva una linterna y una pila de repuesto por si bajas después del anochecer, ya que el sendero no tiene luz en ningún tramo.
teaching.explanationEs: In case + presente: te preparas antes de que pase; no equivale a if. Se usa para prevenir, no para condicionar.
segments: Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down
after dark, since the path is not lit at any point.
teaching.audioText: Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down after dark, since the path is not lit at any point.

teaching.en: You had better turn back if the route is icy, because a fall on this slope could be serious and help is hours away.
teaching.es: Más vale que des la vuelta si la ruta está helada, porque una caída en esta pendiente podría ser grave y la ayuda está a horas de distancia.
teaching.explanationEs: Had better + verbo base, sin to: consejo fuerte con una consecuencia implícita.
segments: You had better turn back if the route is icy, because a
fall on this slope could be serious and help is hours away.
teaching.audioText: You had better turn back if the route is icy, because a fall on this slope could be serious and help is hours away.

teaching.en: A waterproof jacket is worth its weight in gold up here, so take precautions even if the morning looks bright and calm.
teaching.es: Una chaqueta impermeable vale su peso en oro aquí arriba, así que toma precauciones aunque la mañana parezca luminosa y tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: Take precautions = tomar medidas antes de que haya un problema. Even if + presente: aunque, sin will.
segments: A waterproof jacket is worth its weight in gold up here,
so take precautions even if the morning looks bright and calm.
teaching.audioText: A waterproof jacket is worth its weight in gold up here, so take precautions even if the morning looks bright and calm.

teaching.en: It is sensible to rest in the shelter if the storm arrives, and when in doubt, err on the side of caution and wait for the guide.
teaching.es: Es sensato descansar en el refugio si llega la tormenta, y en caso de duda, peca de prudente y espera al guía.
teaching.explanationEs: It is sensible to + verbo: consejo razonable, más suave que had better. Err on the side of caution: elegir lo más seguro.

prompt.es: Elige el aviso que solo permite subir con buena visibilidad.

Do not climb provided that the next marker is hidden.
Do not climb unless you can see the next marker.

feedback.es: Unless equivale a «si no» y lleva la condición en positivo; con otra negación el aviso se contradice.

hint.es: Unless ya significa «si no»: no añadas otra negación.

origin.text: Rule for the summit path: people may go up only when they can see the next marker clearly. In thick cloud, nobody should start the climb.

prompt.es: Escucha a la guía: ¿cuándo se puede salir de la ruta marcada?

choices.text: Only when the guide gives permission.
As long as everyone stays together.

feedback.es: La guía solo permite salir de la ruta marcada si ella lo dice («unless I say so»); mantenerse juntos es la condición para usar el camino alto.

origin.audio: Before we set off, the guide gave the group a short talk. You may use the upper path, she said, provided that everyone stays together, and nobody goes outside the marked route unless I say so. Take a torch in case we come down late, and a waterproof jacket in case the clouds build up, even though the sky is blue now. And finally, you had better start drinking water early, because on a long climb it is too late to begin when you are already tired.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada aviso con la idea que expresa.

feedback.es: In case previene, provided that fija una condición, unless marca una excepción a la prohibición y had better aconseja con fuerza.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso del refugio: ¿qué tono y propósito tiene?

choices.text: Angry: it stops guests from using the refuge at all.
Friendly but firm: it sets conditions for using a shared space.
Casual: it offers tips that nobody has to follow.

feedback.es: Permite cocinar con una condición y pide avisar de los daños: amable pero firme, con normas para un espacio compartido.

origin.text: Notice at the refuge: guests may cook inside as long as the window stays open. Please do not leave the stove alone. It is sensible to keep your boots by the door, and you had better report any damage today, before the next group arrives.

prompt.es: Escucha el aviso y elige qué debe hacer quien no lleve botas buenas.

choices.text: Register twice at the desk before leaving.
Come back down before four o'clock this afternoon.
Choose the easier walk by the lake.

feedback.es: El aviso dice que quien no lleve buenas botas debe elegir el paseo del lago; registrarse y volver a las cuatro son otras normas.

origin.audio: Good morning, everyone. This is the ranger station. The summit path is open today, but only provided that you register at the desk first, and you had better be back by four, because the light goes quickly. Unless you have good boots, please choose the lake walk instead. And in case you meet ice on the way down, turn back: no picture is worth a fall.

prompt.es: Lee el correo del club: ¿qué postura adopta el organizador?

choices.text: He prefers to play safe, even if that means cancelling.
He wants the walk to happen whatever the forecast says.
He leaves the final decision entirely to the members.

feedback.es: Dice que prefiere cancelar un buen día a arriesgar uno malo: elige lo prudente aunque cueste renunciar al plan.

origin.text: Dear members, the club will run the ridge walk on Sunday as long as the forecast holds. I would rather cancel a good day than risk a bad one, so I will send a message on Saturday night. If you have not heard from me, assume we go, but you had better check your phone before you leave home.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lleva un mapa de papel por si se agota la batería.»

feedback.es: In case + presente expresa prevención: llevas el mapa antes de saber si la batería se agotará.

origin.text: The phone signal is weak on the high ground. Take a paper map ___ the battery dies.

prompt.es: Escribe seis avisos de seguridad para una ruta de montaña.

answer.text: Safety notices for the ridge walk. 1. Do not start the climb unless the sky is clear at seven in the morning, because the route becomes hazardous when the rocks are wet. 2. You may walk along the ridge provided that the wind is light, and you may stop at the shelter as long as you leave no rubbish. 3. Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down after dark. 4. Carry a waterproof jacket in case the afternoon storm arrives earlier than the forecast says. 5. You had better turn back if the path is icy, because a fall here is a real danger and help is hours away. 6. When in doubt, err on the side of caution: it is sensible to rest in the shelter and wait for the guide. Take precautions, and enjoy the walk.
accepted: Safety notices for the ridge walk. 1. Do not start the climb unless the sky is clear at seven in the morning, because the route becomes hazardous when the rocks are wet. 2. You may walk along the ridge provided that the wind is light, and you may stop at the shelter as long as you leave no rubbish. 3. Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down after dark. 4. Carry a waterproof jacket in case the afternoon storm arrives earlier than the forecast says. 5. You had better turn back if the path is icy, because a fall here is a real danger and help is hours away. 6. When in doubt, err on the side of caution: it is sensible to rest in the shelter and wait for the guide. Take precautions, and enjoy the walk.

Notice 1: Nobody should go up unless a guide has checked the path that morning, because the rocks can be very slippery. Notice 2: The shelter is open to everyone provided that you leave it clean and tidy. Notice 3: Bring a warm coat and a torch in case the night is cold or you finish late. Notice 4: You had better start early if you want to reach the summit before the clouds arrive. Notice 5: It is safe to cross the bridge as long as it is dry, but if you are not sure, err on the side of caution and use the lower path. Notice 6: Keep your phone charged in case you need help, and take precautions against the wind, since it can change very quickly on the ridge.

feedback.es: Un buen cartel une cada instrucción con una condición en presente: unless para excepciones, provided that o as long as para condiciones, in case para prevenir y had better para aconsejar con fuerza.

origin.text: Eres guía en un sendero que sube por un bosque y termina en una cresta. Escribe un cartel con seis avisos (entre 130 y 200 palabras). Usa unless, provided that o as long as, in case y had better, y nombra en cada aviso un peligro o una medida concreta.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué quiere dejar claro la organizadora al final?

choices.text: That children are not welcome on walks.
That the safety form is a real requirement.
That leaders will sign the form for members.

feedback.es: Al avisar de que el formulario se revisará en cada salida, deja claro que es un requisito real y no una formalidad.

origin.audio: At the club meeting, the organiser explained the new walking policy. Members may join any walk, she said, provided that they sign the safety form, and children may come as long as an adult stays with them. Nobody walks alone unless a leader has approved the route. She ended with a warning: you had better read the form carefully, because it will be checked at the start of every walk.

feedback.es: Waterproof es el adjetivo para una prenda que no deja pasar el agua; in case + presente indica la prevención.
